merger_name: Symal Group - Shamrock Engineering and Equipment

anzsic_codes.name: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction

merger_description:
Symal Group Limited (**Symal Group****)** is proposing to acquire Shamrock Equipment Pty Ltd, Shamrock Civil Engineering Pty Ltd and Phoenix Investments Queensland Pty Ltd and certain assets including plant and equipment (together, **Shamrock Group**) (the **Acquisition**).

Symal Group is a civil construction and engineering services provider across the roads, rail, defence, ports and energy sectors, including demolition, bulk earthworks, site preparation, haulage and tip operations services. Symal Group operates businesses under the Symal, Sycle, Unyte, Searo and Wamarra brands.

Shamrock Group is a civil construction, equipment and engineering services provider across the roads, defence, resources, landfill, public infrastructure, and water and gas sectors, including earthworks, demolition and decontamination services.

determination_table_content.details:
Symal Group Limited (Symal Group) is proposing to acquire
Shamrock Equipment Pty Ltd, Shamrock Civil Engineering Pty Ltd,
Phoenix Investments Queensland Pty Ltd and certain assets
including plant and equipment (together, Shamrock Group) (the
Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABZE(1) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition may be put into effect.

The acquirer, Symal Group is a civil construction and engineering
services provider across the roads, rail, defence, ports and energy
sectors, providing demolition, bulk earthworks, site preparation,
haulage and tip operations services. Symal Group operates
businesses under the Symal, Sycle, Unyte, Searo and Wamarra
brands.
The target, Shamrock Group is a civil construction, equipment and
engineering services provider across the roads, defence, resources,
landfill, public infrastructure, and water and gas sectors, providing
earthworks, demolition and decontamination services.

determination_table_content.item:
Overlap and relationship
between the parties
determination_table_content.details:
The parties overlap in the supply of construction and engineering
services.

When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The market share aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is
not significant under either a broad market, including the supply
of construction and engineering services, or under a narrower
segment of specialised civil contracting such as defence civil
contracting.
• There was no information obtained during the public review
which suggested the merger parties were particularly close
competitors in respect of any narrow segment of construction
and engineering services, such that the Acquisition could cause
competition concerns.
• Post Acquisition, the merged firm would continue to face
competition from multiple alternative suppliers of construction
and engineering services across different sectors.

A notifying party, or other person who has been allowed to do so by
the Australian Competition Tribunal, may apply for review if they are
dissatisfied with the determination. Pursuant to section 100C of the
Act, applications for review of the determination are to be made to
the Australian Competition Tribunal before the end of 14 calendar
days after this statement of reasons was included on the ACCC’s
Acquisitions Register. To confirm whether there has been any
application for review, please contact the Australian Competition
Tribunal.
